profiles.summary: Effort guides how much the model thinks: lower levels favor speed and fewer tokens; higher levels reason more completely. The model does not accept none.
Effort guides reasoning depth; lower levels favor speed and fewer tokens, while higher levels reason more completely. none and minimal are unsupported.
Effort guides reasoning depth; lower levels favor speed and fewer tokens, while higher levels reason more completely.
Effort guides reasoning depth; lower levels favor speed and fewer tokens, while higher levels reason more completely.
Effort guides reasoning depth; lower levels favor speed and fewer tokens, while higher levels reason more completely. The gpt-5.6 alias routes to this Sol tier.
A balance of intelligence and cost. Effort guides reasoning depth; lower levels favor speed and fewer tokens, while higher levels reason more completely.
Designed for cost-sensitive, high-volume workloads. Effort guides reasoning depth; lower levels favor speed and fewer tokens.
Effort tunes reasoning; medium is the balanced default, low favors speed and cost, and high or xhigh are for harder work when evaluations justify the extra latency and cost.
A higher-compute variant for tougher problems. Requests may take several minutes; high is the default and xhigh is available for more compute.
Effort applies to response text, tool calls, and thinking when active. It is a behavioral signal, not a strict token budget; higher levels suit capability-sensitive, long-horizon work.
Effort applies to response text, tool calls, and thinking when active. It is a behavioral signal, not a strict token budget; higher levels suit capability-sensitive work.
Effort affects response text, tool calls, and thinking. Adaptive thinking is always on; effort is the main control for reasoning depth and request cost. The default differs from Opus 5 and earlier.
Effort affects response text, tool calls, and thinking. It is a behavioral signal rather than a strict token budget; high is the documented default for these models.
Effort affects response text, tool calls, and thinking; it is not a strict token budget. The current effort guide lists max but not xhigh for this model.
Effort affects response text, tool calls, and thinking when active. It is a behavioral signal rather than a strict token budget; higher levels suit longer-horizon work.
Effort applies to response text, tool calls, and thinking. The current effort guide lists max but not xhigh for this model.
In the Responses API, effort controls both thinking mode and intensity: none disables thinking; low, high, and max enable it. medium maps to high and minimal maps to low for compatibility.
In the Responses API, effort controls both thinking mode and intensity: none disables thinking; low, high, and max enable it. medium maps to high and minimal maps to low for compatibility.
DeepSeek V4.1-Flash accepts low/high/max, with high as the documented default. These are lab model values; the separate OpenCode Go route registry governs whether an effort field may be inserted.
Thinking is dynamic by default. Low favors latency and cost, medium is balanced, and high maximizes reasoning depth; minimal is unsupported for these models.
Thinking is dynamic by default. Minimal is supported but does not guarantee thinking is fully off; low favors latency and cost, while high maximizes reasoning depth.
Thinking defaults to minimal. Minimal does not guarantee reasoning is fully off; low favors latency and cost, while high maximizes reasoning depth.
Thinking defaults to high and cannot be disabled. Low favors latency and cost, medium is balanced, and high maximizes reasoning depth.
Thinking defaults to minimal; only minimal and high are supported. Minimal does not guarantee thinking is fully off; high maximizes reasoning depth.
Thinking defaults to high. Minimal is not a guarantee that thinking is fully off; low favors latency and cost, while high maximizes reasoning depth.
Thinking defaults to medium. Minimal does not guarantee reasoning is fully off; low favors latency and cost, while high maximizes reasoning depth.
Thinking defaults to minimal. Minimal does not guarantee reasoning is fully off; low favors latency and cost, while high maximizes reasoning depth.
The Live API model supports configurable background reasoning at low, medium, or high. The guide does not specify a default level.
Thinking defaults to high. Minimal does not guarantee reasoning is fully off; low favors latency and cost, while high maximizes reasoning depth.
Effort controls reasoning depth and cannot disable reasoning. High is the default; xhigh is available on Grok 4.6 and later for maximum depth at greater latency.
Effort controls reasoning depth and cannot disable reasoning. High is the default; xhigh is not a distinct setting on Grok 4.5 and is treated as high.
Here reasoning.effort controls how many agents collaborate, rather than reasoning depth. The documentation does not state a default level.
Thinking is enabled by default and can be disabled. OpenAI-compatible reasoning_effort exposes only none/high; a separate token_budget caps thinking tokens rather than providing graded effort levels.

The model guide confirms reasoning_effort is adjustable and explicitly describes none/high; high surfaces a thinking chunk at increased token use. Model-specific defaults and support for other values are not listed.

The model guide confirms reasoning_effort is adjustable and explicitly describes none/high; high surfaces a thinking chunk at increased token use. Model-specific defaults and support for other values are not listed.
This router selects a free model at random and may choose a different underlying model per request. No stable target-model effort levels or default can be documented for the router ID.
A reasoning-first research and forecasting model. Its research paper describes capabilities but no discrete request effort levels or default.
Structured System One decision model returning typed probabilities rather than generated chat. No model-specific reasoning-effort levels are documented.
A behavior-scoring model that returns probabilities for requested conversation behaviors. Its API guide documents scoring, not reasoning-effort controls.
Medical-reasoning Ling 3.0 Flash variant. Its model card describes reasoning and agent capabilities but no discrete request effort levels or default.
Text embedding model for retrieval and semantic search; it returns vectors rather than generated responses. Reasoning effort does not apply.
Multimodal model for reasoning, coding, long-context work, and agent workflows. Its model card does not publish discrete request effort levels or a default.
Compact reasoning model for agent workflows, extraction, and retrieval. The model guidance describes capabilities but no discrete request effort levels or default.
High-throughput agentic language model. NVIDIA's model card does not document discrete reasoning-effort levels or a default for this model.
Smaller multimodal Inkling model for general reasoning, coding, and agent use. Its model card documents no discrete request effort levels or default.
Speech-synthesis model variant for generating audio, not a text reasoning target. Its API announcement documents no effort levels.
Coding-agent model for software engineering and long-horizon tasks. Its model documentation does not publish discrete request effort levels or a default.
Multimodal model for reasoning, coding, tool use, and agent workflows. Its model card documents no discrete request effort levels or default.
Text embedding model for enterprise search and retrieval; it returns vectors rather than generated responses. Reasoning effort does not apply.
Compact coding-agent model with tool use and reasoning capabilities. Its documentation does not publish discrete request effort levels or a default.
Agentic coding model with interleaved reasoning and tool use. Cohere's announcement documents no discrete request effort levels or default.
Multimodal reranker scoring query-document relevance, not a generative reasoning model. Discrete reasoning effort does not apply.
Multimodal content-moderation model with a reasoning-mode toggle. The model card does not document graded effort levels or a default.
Frontier reasoning and orchestration model for long-running agent workflows. NVIDIA's report does not publish request effort levels or a default.
Multimodal perception and reasoning model. OpenRouter describes extended thinking as enabled via a boolean; no discrete effort levels or default are documented.
Multimodal instruction model with configurable thinking mode. Google documents a prompt-level thinking toggle, not a discrete effort-level enum.
Multimodal instruction model with configurable thinking mode. Google documents a prompt-level thinking toggle, not a discrete effort-level enum.
Open hybrid model for multi-agent applications and long-context reasoning. NVIDIA's model report does not document discrete request effort levels or a default.
Multimodal embedding model for visual document retrieval; it returns vectors rather than generated responses. Reasoning effort does not apply.
Thinking is always on. GLM-5.3 accepts low, high, and max reasoning effort; max is the documented default.
Thinking is always on. GLM-5.3-Flash accepts low, high, and max reasoning effort; max is the documented default.
GLM-5.2 documents none/minimal/low/medium/high/xhigh/max, default max. none/minimal skip thinking; low/medium map to high and xhigh maps to max.
These versions support the thinking toggle, but the guide says they auto-determine whether to think and documents no graded reasoning-effort levels for them.
The guide describes thinking as forced when enabled for GLM-4.7 and GLM-4.5V. It documents no graded reasoning-effort levels for these versions.
These Z.ai multimodal GLM variants are listed in the parameter guide; no model-specific discrete reasoning-effort levels or default are documented.
Kimi K3 always reasons. The API accepts reasoning_effort low/high/max, with max as the documented default.
K2.7 Code always thinks and does not support reasoning_effort. Its highspeed variant has the same documented thinking behavior.
Kimi K2.6 thinking is enabled by default and can be disabled with thinking.type. Its API does not support discrete reasoning_effort levels.
LongCat documents a thinking.type enabled/disabled toggle, not discrete effort levels. LongCat-2.5-Preview thinking is enabled by default; OpenCode Go exposes it as longcat-2.5-preview-free.
These MiMo models support a thinking.type enabled/disabled toggle, enabled by default. Xiaomi's API guide documents no discrete reasoning-effort levels for this family.
M3 thinking is off by default on the Anthropic API and can be enabled with adaptive mode. M2.7 cannot disable thinking. The docs list no discrete effort values for either model.
Contributor tiers support minimal through xhigh reasoning effort. none is rejected; max is available only on standard Muse Spark 1.3, not Contributor models.
Thinking is enabled by default. reasoning.effort accepts low/medium/xhigh; minimal maps to low, high/max map to xhigh, and none disables thinking.
Alibaba lists thinking as enabled by default and supports reasoning.effort on the Responses API, but its guide does not give this model a specific accepted-level set.
Tencent lists both models as supporting deep thinking. The model catalog documents no discrete reasoning-effort values or default level.
OpenCode Go lists Space Bunny, but the upstream lab and its effort documentation are not public. No model-specific effort levels are asserted.
